title: Agreed!
subtitle: Four ways to say yes
review: Text by the author; notes and questions written by Claude: check them. No Burmese yet.
intro: A deal about the dishes, a haircut nobody noticed, a bookshelf built without the instructions and a morning run that turns into croissants: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for how they say yes, and for the moments when yes means 'I don't believe you'.

lines.text: Tonight, I'll cook and you do the dishes. Deal?

lines.note: Sounds good: a casual yes to a plan.

lines.text: Maybe. But there won't be any dishes to wash.

lines.note: You've got a deal = I accept.
After a negative question, answer with the verb: Of course I do!
It suits me = it looks good on me.

lines.text: Definitely. That's exactly what I was going to say.
You've got six screws left over.

lines.note: True = you're right about that. Extras: more than you need.

lines.text: That's intentional. It's a design feature.

lines.note: Yeah, right… is sarcastic. It means 'I don't believe you'.

lines.text: Okay, you're right. Where are the instructions?
Under the bookshelf. To keep it level.
Tomorrow, I'm getting up at six to go for a run.

lines.note: If you say so…: I don't believe it, but I won't argue.

lines.text: I'm serious! I've set my alarm. Wanna come?
lines.note: Wanna = want to. Spoken only: do not write it.

lines.text: Actually, we could start with the croissants.

lines.note: Totally: informal strong agreement. Skip: not do.
Now you're talking! = that's a much better idea.

notes: Deal, Sounds good and Agreed say yes to a plan.
Absolutely, Definitely and Totally are strong. Totally is informal.
You're right and True accept the other person's point.
Tone can reverse the meaning: Yeah, right… and If you say so… mean 'I don't believe you'.
After a negative question, answer with the verb: Don't you notice anything? — Of course I do!
Now you're talking! welcomes a better idea.

questions.q: Emma suggests switching jobs tomorrow. Lucas accepts casually. What does he say?
questions.why: Sounds good is a casual yes to a plan.

questions.q: Lucas says the leaning bookshelf is 'a design feature'. Emma does not believe him. What does she say?
questions.why: Yeah, right… is sarcastic: 'I don't believe you'.

questions.q: Lucas finally accepts that he should read the instructions. What does he say?
questions.why: You're right accepts the other person's point.

questions.q: Lucas says he will get up at six. Emma doubts it. What does she say?
questions.why: If you say so… = I don't believe it, but I won't argue.
